sowhat.text: EQT-Range shows large stock-for-stock deals getting done in gas with the 10-year at 5.00%, while sponsors face pricier, more selective leveraged finance. Oil near $116 Brent keeps energy dealmaking active.

pitch: Stocks bounced on Monday. The S&P rose about 0.7 percent, led by chips after Anthropic's IPO filing revived the AI trade. Oil eased a little on Middle East talks, but Brent is still around 116 dollars, near six-month highs. The 10-year is flat at 5 percent, and the Fed meets Wednesday with futures pricing about a 92 percent chance of a hold at 3.75 to 4. On M&A, EQT agreed to buy Range Resources in an all-stock deal creating a gas producer with over 50 billion dollars of enterprise value, and Ovintiv is buying Logan Energy for about 1.3 billion. Financing is open but more selective, with spreads near 340 basis points on high yield.

quiz.a: Evercore (lead) and J.P. Morgan; EQT used Citi and RBC.

chat.q: What's your read on oil right now?
chat.a: Brent settled at $115.81 and WTI at $101.76, both down slightly on Monday after Friday's jump. Mediation hopes pulled prices back while Houthi attacks on Saudi pipelines kept them near six-month highs. High prices support cash flow for producers, which helps funding for energy M&A like EQT-Range and Ovintiv-Logan.
chat.tip: Name the spread: Brent about $14 above WTI.

chat.a: EQT agreed to buy Range Resources in an all-stock deal, 0.987 EQT shares per Range share, creating a company with over $50B of pro forma enterprise value. Citi and RBC advised EQT; Evercore and J.P. Morgan advised Range. It shows gas consolidation getting done in stock rather than cash, which sidesteps a 5% 10-year.

chat.q: What are you watching this week?
chat.a: The Fed decision Wednesday, where futures give about a 92% chance of a hold at 3.75–4.00%. Then Microsoft and Alphabet earnings for AI capex signals, and Thursday's GDP and core PCE. Together they set the rate and risk backdrop for financing.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The discount rate rises, so present value falls, and terminal value falls most because it is the long-dated piece. With the 10-year at 5.00% now, the risk-free rate is already high, so a further 50 bp would cut equity values for long-duration assets and make leveraged buyouts harder to finance.
chat.tip: State direction, then the terminal value point.

chat.q: Why would EQT pay in stock for Range?
chat.a: An all-stock deal keeps the balance sheet clean when borrowing is expensive, with the 10-year at 5.00% and high-yield spreads near 338 bp. Range holders get 27% of the combined company and share in synergies, which EQT put at $325M within two years. The tradeoff is dilution and the need for both shareholder votes.

chat.q: How would you describe credit markets today?
chat.a: Open but selective. High-yield spreads were 338 bp and IG 91 bp at the 23 Oct reading, which is tight by history, but Octus reported some deals needed structure changes and data center bonds were paused. Strong credits like Crescent Energy's $1.5B loan still priced.
chat.tip: Give both sides: tight spreads, picky buyers.
